functions.//: The WebAuthn relying party, and nothing else. Every function is capped with maxInstances in src/config.ts — Blaze bills by invocation, and an uncapped function is what turns a runaway into a bill.

rewrites.//: The catch-all below swallows everything, /.well-known/* included, which is why neither platform-association file was reachable. These two come first — within `rewrites`, Hosting applies the first rule whose pattern matches. The files themselves live in web/well-known/ (no leading dot) because the `ignore` glob `**/.*` drops any dotted directory before deploy, so a real web/.well-known/ would never be uploaded at all.

headers.//: Apple fetches this with no file extension and requires application/json. Android's assetlinks.json gets the type from its extension, but is pinned here too so neither depends on Hosting guessing. Both are declared against the /.well-known/ request path, not the rewritten one.

Flutter web output is NOT content-hashed — main.dart.js keeps the same filename every build — so a long immutable max-age would pin browsers to the version they first loaded and no redeploy would reach them. But plain 'no-cache' is worse: Firebase Hosting stops honouring If-None-Match on it and re-sends the whole ~1 MB gzipped bundle on every page load. 'max-age=0, must-revalidate' is the pair that works: revalidate before every use, and get a 304 when the build has not changed.
canvaskit is pinned to the Flutter SDK version, so it may be held longer.
